budgetEnforcement.modelRequests: Hard allowance at actual provider.decide entry; SDK reservations may also count a denied call.
budgetEnforcement.rounds: Hard allowance at createSession entry; resuming an existing session consumes no new slot; a failed creation still consumes its call slot.
budgetEnforcement.actions: Soft threshold using distinct SDK action.started IDs, reconciled against the final attempt ledger. An in-flight recovery may dispatch multiple internal attempts and exceed it; no attempt hooks or session budgets are changed.
budgetEnforcement.durationMs: Provider/session entries check the deadline and a timer requests pause. Already started SDK work, including an entire recovery call, settles normally and may exceed the window.
budgetEnforcement.progress: Unkeyed successful exploration is reported separately and defers repeated-route/no-progress guards for this window while that success remains valid.

metricLimits: Actual successful attempts and newly resolved plan rows are separate; neither deduplicates all semantic operations.
browserOperationKey is a scheduling hint: same-name/shared-identifier targets can still collide. Candidate keys grant no identity, uniqueness, or scope completion.
Missing targets, unresolved identity or unavailable conditions are unkeyed; such successes defer no-progress and repeated-route guards.
Provider counts are actual decide calls, not billable HTTP requests; usage only includes parsed provider answers.
Necessary reentry is a candidate backed by route evidence and requires child-progress review.
Repeated-route and no-progress guards identify review candidates, not a proof that every retry was unnecessary.
Partial live integrity audits rotate through eight protected artifacts; startup/settled audits check all protected artifacts.
Raw decisions, observations, unknown attempts and request ledgers remain in the owned databases.
